transcript_class: CAPTURE-TIME VERBATIM RECORD — paste of the Overview expanded, with its source cards
d: THE GETTY PROVENANCE INDEX, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'an open-access digital database maintained by the Getty Research Institute that provides over 12 million records tracking the ownership, circulation, display, and transfer of artworks.' Scope (12 million linked open data records on the Arches platform; archival inventories, auction catalogues and dealer stock books; the Knoedler and Goupil stock books; sales catalogues from roughly the sixteenth to the twentieth century), searchable categories, and the search portal. An image strip ('View all') heads the paste. Nine cards: three Getty pages, Princeton's guide to the legacy database, the GitHub CSV exports, CNI, USC Libraries, ARIAH (the relaunch), Smarthistory.
reading: The innocent reading first. The Overview identifies the index, its maintainer and its scale, says what documents it draws on and how to search it.
findings: THE INDEX HELD. 'over 12 million' resources, the Getty Research Institute and the move to linked open data are the record's. Checked 2026-10-29 against the provenance census record of the same day and the sources it saved.

THE FOUNDING UNSAID, AND WITH IT THE CONFLICT. The record holds two founding statements from the Getty's own pages: 'Founded in 1974 by Burton Fredericksen' and 'began as an initiative within the Getty Museum’s Paintings department in the early 1980s led by curator Burton B. Fredericksen'. The composition gives neither, and names no person.

THE STOCK BOOKS. 'the 11 painting stock books of the New York dealership M. Knoedler & Co. and Goupil & Cie (covering 1872–1970)' joins two dealers' books under one count and one span. The Getty's coverage page, which the record saved, gives M. Knoedler & Co. (New York, 1872–1970) the 11 painting stock books and Goupil & Cie./Boussod, Valadon & Cie (Paris, 1846–1919) 15 stock books of their own. The composition also gives the sales catalogues the whole Index's span ('roughly from the 16th century through the 20th century'). (Repaired 2026-10-29: the finding had left the join unchecked.)

THE LEGACY AND THE COVERAGE. The record's lifecycle (archival inventories still on the legacy platform during the transition) and its negative tag (coverage varies by region, period and type of document) are absent; the Princeton card's date ranges are the legacy database's.
analysis: The index of provenance is composed with its scale and maintainer right and its own origin left out. The founder is the person most associated with the index on the Getty's pages; the composition gives the institution and leaves the person in the archive.
per_note: The Getty Research Institute, Knoedler and Goupil named; no person; no identifier; the Getty's own pages cited.

originator.name: Getty Research Institute (J. Paul Getty Trust)
originator.basis: Not the archive's: Getty Provenance Index; its operator, as the record gives it: Getty Research Institute (J. Paul Getty Trust). Formalized by the provenance meta-aggregator record of 2026-10-29 (https://www.provenanceerasure.org/aggregators/getty-provenance-index/), editor Lee Sharks; the record's fields carry verbatim quotes from the sources it saved with sha256, each with its basis (the operator's own page or a third-party account).
